correctness.rationale: Counting marked cycles gives the exact two factorial moments under a uniform derangement. The alternating-series lemma is proved for all integer shifts, with careful handling of the zero a_1; it yields strict sign for every n>=r+s. Independent exact enumeration through n=8 and 27,237 assertions in verify.py corroborate the finite identities but are not used as an infinite proof. Cases r+s>n, n=r, n-1 boundaries are separately specified.

originality.rationale: The 2020 derangement paper already contains general factorial moments; those exact moment formulas are not new. The distinct claim is the strict sign pattern of the two-length covariance for every admissible finite size, including a universal alternating-sign determinant inequality and the sharp first nonzero factorial term. Inspected relevant primary sections and targeted literature/index searches have not found this strict sign-and-rate theorem. Although an older implicit proof remains possible, the explicit joint moment formula alone is not a strict-sign classification without the alternating-determinant argument.
residual_risks: 2020 factorial-moment identity explicitly covers the exact covariance values; the originality claim is only the previously unidentified strict global sign classification and sharp coefficient.
Another source might already establish the same alternating determinant inequality under an analytic-sequence name.
A broad all-purpose formula can make the present sign rule a derived corollary; independent priority review remains necessary.

value.rationale: Two cycle-size counts are uncorrelated in unconditioned uniform permutations when they can coexist, but fixed-point exclusion induces covariance with an exact parity flip at every increment of the residual sample size. The theorem resolves a natural finite-sample dependence question uniformly over all two cycle lengths and quantifies its sharp factorial disappearance. This is more than a single finite table entry or numerical correction.
